chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Hind al-Ḥannāṭ, who said:
I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) say: Whoever visits al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) knowing his right, following him, Allāh will forgive him his past and future sins.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for the forgiveness of sins through visiting Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh highlights that the efficacy of visiting Imām al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) hinges on 'irfān bi-ḥaqqihi' (knowing his specific rights and status), a concept central to Shia theological epistemology. This condition ensures the visitation is not merely physical but a profound spiritual alignment with the Imam’s authority, resulting in the comprehensive forgiveness of sins. The emphasis on 'knowing' reflects the Shia view that correct belief (‘aqīdah) and recognition (ma‘rifah) are prerequisites for valid worship.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 6. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Hind Al-Ḥannāť, who said:
I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: Allāh will forgive all of the past and future sins of those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.) knowing his rights and believing in his Imamate.
